text:
maria: Heads up: us-west-3 is showing recurring 'writewave' events on scratch NVMe that correlate with GPU attach failures over the last 2 hours. Seeing thermal fan fallback + firmware retry loop in SMART logs. Anyone digging in?

kevin: On it. I see attach_errors spike at 02:13 and 02:37. Here's tail of node logs:
```
node=gpu-23 scrubber=janitor write_latency=324ms fan_state=fallback fw_retry=3 attach_error=ENXIO
[2025-11-02T02:13:21Z] nvme0: write delayed, temp=78C, pcie_link_retrain=1
```

sophie: Is this the same pattern as last month? Thermal + retransmit causing write amplification? Could be cleaner concurrency colliding with GPU batch launches.

maria: Not identical — last month was firmware-rollback. This one has sustained write tail with periodic 'corrupt marker' flags from SMART. No full drive failures yet.

samir: @kevin can you check janitor concurrency and fstrim window? If cleaner/trim jobs line up with batch GPU launches we overload IO.

kevin: Checked. Janitor concurrency on those nodes was 6 (default). Two heavy batch launches coincided. Proposing reduce concurrency to 2 for us-west-3 rainy window. Also throttle fstrim to 10s spacing.

sophie: :thumbsup: Also suggest a temporary routing rule to prefer dedicated pool fallback for attaches when node write_latency > 200ms. That'd keep customer allocs from failing.

maria: Agreed. Ops: can we push a rolling policy? infra-bot, can we get a metric alert rule for 'writewave' pattern? Maybe look for 3x write_latency spikes + fan_state fallback within 30m.

infra-bot: Created alert rule 'WRITEWAVE_USW3' -> triggers on host.write_latency_p95 > 200ms && host.fan_state == fallback over 30m. Notified channel eng-oncall plus runbook link: https://go/runbooks/writewave

kevin: I'll run a targeted janitor config roll on 10% of nodes now: command snippet
```
for node in $(list nodes --label us-west-3 --limit 10); do
  kubectl annotate node $node janitor.concurrency=2
done
```

samir: If we go this path, need cost callout: reduced concurrency increases backlog and may delay garbage collection, raising temp storage usage. We should increase ephemeral retention by +1h to avoid OOM on batch jobs.

sophie: Noted. I'll queue a canary routing change to prefer fallback pool for attaches with latency>200ms. low-risk rollback in 10m.

maria: Can we also get telemetry for 'corrupt markers' exported to S3 for triage? want a quick grep of firmware logs.

kevin: Dump scheduled. Also kicking vendor support ticket with SSD vendor — attaching logs. Ticket #RDW-8402

sophie: Can someone post short postmortem if this recurs? Also ping oncall to watch next 6 hours. :eyes: 

maria: Thanks team. Will follow up with impact metrics in 30m. Temporary mitigations: janitor concurrency -> 2, routing fallback canary -> enabled, retention +1h.
